catalog_quote: 2.1. Le pied. L’élément prosodique principal du mwan est le pied, unité d’un niveau supérieur à la syllabe, cf. (Vydrine 2005; 2010). C’est l’unité prosodique qui peut se composer d’une ou deux syllabes qui se comportent phonétiquement comme une structure unique. Le pied en mwan est porteur du ton; il est caractérisé aussi par la nasalité / oralité et l’harmonie des voyelles ... Le mwan a les types de pieds suivants : V, VV, CV, CVV, CvLV, CVŋ, CvLvŋ. ... 2.4. Les tons. La langue mwan comporte trois tons phonologiques de base : haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B). Dans la transcription scientifique, les tons sont désignés par des signes diacritiques : le ton haut par l’accent aigu (v́); le ton moyen par le macron (v̄); le ton bas par l’accent grave (v̀). Exemples de triplets minimaux : kùè ‘ratel’, kūē ‘néré’, kúé ‘fardeau’; kàà ‘lime’; kāā ‘poisson’, káá ‘gratter’. Les pieds de types …

audit.recode_to: kind 'tonal' unchanged. Add Perekhvalskaya 2017 p.720 §2.1.2 ('Ударение в М.я. отсутствует.') as a second deciding source: stress is now explicitly denied, so domain should move from UNSTATED to 'no word stress (explicitly stated)'; if the catalog convention (per the second reader's note) codes a tonal language with an explicit denial of stress as NO-WORD-STRESS rather than TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT, change qv accordingly — otherwise keep TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT and cite the denial in the rule/notes.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the held OpenEdition full text at the stated paragraphs. (2) Deciding source is a 2018 dictionary front-matter phonology sketch by the language's main describer: authoritative on tone (3 level tones, foot as tone domain, sandhi classes) but silent on stress, which is why the record hedged domain=UNSTATED. (3) Glottolog's top-ranked item, Perekhvalskaya 2017 'Muan jazyk' (Jazyki mira: Mande, 48 pp grammar), was fetched sources openly from the RAS Institute of Linguistics site; p.720 §2.1.2 says in one sentence that Mwan has no stress, then gives the H/M/L tone system with tonal series (p.721), tone bearer = syllable, grammatical tone, limited intonation. Her 2022 'Tonal paradigms in Mwan' (SPbU proceedings, p.17) repeats the three-level-tone analysis. Both agree with 'tonal'; the 2017 chapter sharpens the record from 'stress unmentioned' to 'stress explicitly absent

sources.citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena V. 2022. Tonal paradigms in Mwan. In: Proceedings of the International Congress on Historiography and Source Studies of Asia and Africa, vol. 2, part 2, 12ff. St. Petersburg State University.
sources.quote: 'There are three level tones in Mwan: high (v́), middle (v̄) and low (v̀). Examples of minimal triples: kùè 'badger', kūē 'wing bean (tree)', kúé 'load' ...'; tone-changing patterns by left tonal context; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena V. 2017. Muan jazyk [Mwan]. In V.F. Vydrin, Ju.V. Mazurova, A.A. Kibrik & E.B. Markus (eds.), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 718-765. St. Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija. (whole-volume PDF linked from iling-ran.ru/web/ru/publications/langworld/volumes/21)
sources.quote: '2.1.2. Ударение в М.я. отсутствует. В М.я. выделяются три основных фонологических (смыслоразличительных) тона: высокий, средний и низкий.' [Stress is absent in Mwan. Three basic phonological tones are distinguished: high, mid and low.] Further (p. 721): 'Носитель тона — слог (гласная)'; grammatical tones (habitual = all-mid); intonation functions limited; nasalization is a foot-level prosody. Also discusses and rejects Bolli & Flik's falling tone on long vowels (treated as H+L).
sources.locator: p. 720, §2.1.2 (continuing onto p. 721, Table 1 'Примеры тональных серий')
